dashboard.market_summary: The dominant macro narrative today is stagflationary deterioration: structural inflation expected to settle in the 3.5–4.5% range is colliding with deteriorating consumer fundamentals and slowing demand, creating a hostile environment for both equities and long-duration bonds. All three sources converge on avoiding long-duration bond exposure in favor of short-duration T-bills, while the S&P 500 has broken below its 50-day moving average with the 200-DMA (~7,001) now a credible downside target. AI/megacap tech faces a specific double threat — capital-intensive spending suppressing near-term productivity gains while deferred capex depreciation risks cratering free cash flow even as reported earnings look optically healthy. Against this backdrop, hard assets and precious metals emerge as the clearest structural beneficiary, supported by both the inflationary thesis (Thoughtful Money) and macro dislocation hedging (Eurodollar University). Industrial commodities benefit directionally from the same inflationary tailwind but lack strong dedicated source coverage today, warranting a more cautious sizing.

ai_tech.rationale: Two sources flag meaningful headwinds — AI capital intensity is inflationary rather than disinflationary near-term, and hyperscaler free cash flow is projected to collapse 91% as depreciation hits, pressuring valuations. However, the explicit tactical guidance is to hold at target weight rather than sell outright until hyperscaler earnings reports provide confirmation, making a full exit premature.

precious_metals.rationale: Both Thoughtful Money and Eurodollar University — despite disagreeing on whether inflation or disinflation dominates — converge on hard assets and physical gold as the appropriate macro hedge; in a stagflationary scenario, precious metals serve as protection against both currency debasement and institutional policy error. This is today's strongest cross-source bullish signal and aligns with the stealth QE and structural inflation thesis.

industrial_commodities.rationale: Industrial commodities are flagged as beneficiaries of the new inflationary structural environment alongside precious metals, but direct source coverage is thin and the simultaneous demand-destruction risk from stagflation (weak consumer, slowing growth) tempers the bullish case. A hold is appropriate — directional tailwind exists but conviction is insufficient to add aggressively at this stage.

macro.rationale: All three sources converge on a bearish macro view — stagflation, consumer deterioration, and a potential surprise Fed rate hike (34% market-implied probability) create a risk-off backdrop; the recommended posture is defensive, favoring short-duration T-bills over risk assets. Investors should reduce long-duration bond exposure and broadly trim cyclical risk until macro clarity improves.
